scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9012: The partner network is REALLY slow today from my
machine (pc1) -- getting anything from their side (pc2, 200.1.1.2) takes
ages, even if it does eventually respond. Yesterday it was snappy, so
something has changed on your side. I don't understand the connection
between our two companies and I shouldn't have to -- slow is slow. Find out
why and get it back to normal today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 with 0% loss and low, stable RTT -- the peering is not congested.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "high latency / congestion" symptom that is false -- does the agent measure RTT
  on the live path, or confabulate a congested peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- high latency / congestion on the peering -- is NOT reproducible: pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss and low, stable round-trip
time. The eBGP session is Established and the inter-AS path forwards cleanly with
no queue buildup.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: latency is low and stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a
sustained ping pc1->pc2, observes low stable RTT, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the peering congested or restarting
router1/router2 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A complete four-phase diagnostic sweep of the simple_bgp topology found no fault mechanism at any layer.

**Affected component:** None identified. All subsystems are operating normally.

**Mechanism examined:** (1) L2 identity — infra_sweep and l2_snapshot confirmed zero ACL/firewall drop rules, zero duplicate MAC addresses, all 4 devices with correct IPs and default routes, and ARP entries healthy on both hosts. (2) BGP control plane — bgp_snapshot confirmed FRR daemons (watchfrr, zebra, bgpd) active on both routers, BGP sessions Established, router1 (AS 1) advertising 195.11.14.0/24 and router2 (AS 2) advertising 200.1.1.0/24. (3) Traffic shaping — tc_snapshot inspected all 6 interfaces and found only the kernel-default fq_codel qdisc on each; no TBF rate limiter, no netem delay/corruption/jitter was present. (4) Resource pressure — pressure_sweep found no stress or flood tools, no CPU spikes, and no abnormal socket counts on any device. (5) Routing tables confirmed BGP-learned routes are FIB-installed in both directions with correct next-hops (193.10.11.1↔193.10.11.2).

**Localization:** No device or interface is implicated.

**Root cause:** There is no current network fault; topology-wide reachability shows 0 % loss and sub-millisecond RTT (~0.9 ms pc1→pc2) at the time of investigation.

**Fix:** No corrective action is needed. The reported "slowness" is not reproducible or measurable in the live lab state. The incident may have been transient or application-layer in origin, and has left no network-level trace.
